questions.question: Where should tokkit take the PR-open time from?

options.label: GitHub createdAt (Recommended)
options.description: Pass --pr <N>; the kit asks gh for the PR's createdAt and splits the phases at that time. Exact, and immune to reused branch names. The cost: measuring needs network access, or a cached JSON file next to the snapshot.

options.label: The gh pr create call
options.description: Use the timestamp of the transcript's own `gh pr create` call (or its MCP equivalent). Works offline, but misses PRs opened by another session or by hand.

options.label: Filter pr-link by number
options.description: Keep pr-link records but take only the one whose prNumber matches a --pr argument. The smallest change; it still trusts a record Claude Code writes for its own reasons.

questions.question: What marks the end of orient + plan?

options.label: The approval answer (Recommended)
options.description: The first approved ExitPlanMode result, or failing that the answer to the orient-scope AskUserQuestion. This matches the /ship flow, where scope is approved before planning ends.

options.label: First Edit to a tracked file
options.description: Keep the first-edit rule but ignore writes under tmp/, the scratchpad and the sandbox. It doesn't depend on which dialog tool was used, but it is still a guess about intent.

options.label: Explicit --plan-end flag
options.description: The person measuring passes a timestamp or call index. Always right, but done by hand, which is what the roadmap wants to stop.

questions.question: Should this PR also fix commit detection (`git -C <dir> commit`)?

options.label: Yes, same PR (Recommended)
options.description: It's the third defect the BK-424 body names, a one-line normalisation in tool_label. Leaving it out leaves the item partly undone.

options.label: Dates only
options.description: Fix only the two phase boundaries and file commit detection as a separate follow-up.

questions.question: Orient found two related open items. BK-431 constrains BK-424: it will compare its phase table against run B, so the phase rows and JSON keys must stay comparable. BK-417 is unrelated: it covers a different script with its own constants. Scope?

options.label: BK-424 alone (Recommended)
options.description: Cover the three defects plus the `pr-link`-based search for related sessions, which has the same root cause: pass `--pr` and it uses that PR. BK-431 and BK-417 stay open and untouched.

options.label: BK-424 + BK-417
options.description: Also fix report_token_usage.py's constants. A different script and audience, and it widens what the review has to read.

questions.question: The kit has never had tests (#1098, #1102 and #1111 shipped none). How should this fix be checked?

options.label: Synthetic tests + run B (Recommended)
options.description: Add tests/scripts/test_tokkit.py with small hand-built transcripts covering pr-link vs --pr, plan approval, a rejected plan, and `git -C` and `-c` commits. Also run the kit on run B's snapshot and check for 44 / 49 / 2 calls. The run B check stays local because the snapshot holds prompts.

options.label: Run B only
options.description: Follow the kit's precedent: no committed test, just run the kit on run B's snapshot and record 44 / 49 / 2 in the trace and PR. Cheaper, but nothing guards the boundaries later.

questions.question: What should `report` do when it's run without `--pr`?

options.label: No PR split, say so (Recommended)
options.description: Every call before the plan approval is orient + plan, and everything after it is build. The report prints a line saying to pass --pr to split off the review loop. It never guesses.

options.label: Require --pr
options.description: `report` fails without it. Strict, but a session that never opened a PR can't be reported.

options.label: Fall back to pr-link, warn
options.description: Keep the old source when --pr is missing and print a warning. This keeps the source that misled run B available.
